caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 72 of 1988
lawyer:
SS Halder with Mokhlesur Rahman, Advocates ----- For the Appellants
Awlad Ali, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No. 1
parties:
Meherun Hossain and others ----- Appellants
Vs
Nazrul Islam and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque, J.: This appeal by the defendant appellants is against judgment and decree dated 28.4.1988 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 143 of 1984 decreeing plaintiff respondent No. 1's suit for specific performance of a contract for sale. 

 3. The suit was contested by the minor defendant Nos. 2-4 by filing a joint written statement through their guardian mother defendant No. 1 stating, inter alia, that defendant No. 1 had no power or authority to enter into an agreement to sell the suit property at the time mentioned in the plaint and allegation of extension of the agreement for sale is totally false and the alleged execution is illegal; that plaintiffs claimed agreement having been executed without permission of the court is not legally binding on the defendant Nos. 2-4; that though defendant No. 1 has been shown as one of the executants she did not execute the same for herself but on behalf of the minor defendant Nos. 2-4 illegally without any authority and said illegal agreement was cancelled by the defendant No. 1 by notice; that allegation of partition of the suit premises and falling of the suit property in the exclusive Saham of the defendants and the plaintiffs being a tenant under the defendants in room No.3 is not correct; that the plaintiff is a tenant under Hossain Banu widow of late Hafiz Md. Hossain and became defaulter and got the alleged agreement executed by the defendant No. 1 on false representation for saving him from ejectment due to his being defaulter; that the plaintiff acted against the interest of the minors by forcibly occupying land beyond the alleged suit land and making constructions, that the purpose for which proposal to transfer minors property was given no longer exists; that the minors failed to purchase land for their residence due to fraud, cheating and violation of agreement by the plaintiff; that the alleged agreement is against the interest and welfare of the minors and as such plaintiff is not entitled to specific performance thereof. 

 5. Court below decreed the suit on consideration of evidence on record holding that the defendant No. 1 executed the agreement Ext. 1 for herself and on behalf of her minor children on receipt of Tk. 1,00,000.00 as earnest money and as such the deed of agreement is genuine and valid and there is no legal bar in enforcing the same. 

 6. Mr. SS Halder, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submitted that under the Mohammedan Law mother is not the legal guardian of her minor children and as such she has no power to enter into an agreement to sell immovable property of her minor children though they are under her custody and as such the agreement Ext. 1 is void and cannot be enforced against the minors and in support of his contention he relied on some decisions. Mr. Aulad Ali, learned Advocate appearing for plaintiff respondent submitted that in view of the subsequent appointment of the mother defendant No. 1 as certificated guardian of the minor defendant Nos. 2-4 and court's permission to sell the suit property in pursuance of the agreement for sale Ext. 1 defect, if any, in the said agreement was cured by the conduct of the defendant No. 1 and by ratification. He also relied on some decisions in support of his contention. 

 7. Before considering respective submission of the parties it is necessary to mention that the court below noticed that the defendant No. 1 did not file any written statement on her behalf and as such decreed the suit ex parte against her. We do not find anything to interfere with the said finding of the court below. 

 In the written statement of the defendant Nos.2-4 execution of the deed of agreement Ext. 1 by defendant No. 1 on their behalf has been admitted but payment of Tk. 1,00,000.00 by the plaintiff as earnest money to defendant No. 1 under the said agreement has not been specifically denied though DW 1 denied to have received the same on her deposition. On the other hand plaintiff as PW 1 stated that he paid Tk. 1,00,000.00 as earnest money to the defendant No. 1 and he is corroborated in this respect by PW 3 Md. Yakub Ali, a co-tenant in the suit premises. We, therefore, find nothing to disagree with the court below that defendant No. 1 executed the agreement Ext 1 on receipt of Tk. 1,00,000.00 as earnest money. 

 10. Power of a mother, having charge of the person and property of her minor children without being their guardian appointed by the court, under the Mohammedan Law, to convey to another any right, title or interest in immoveable property has been decided by the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the case of lmambandi Vs. Mutsuddi reported in 45 IA 73. Following that decision Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the case of Md. Ejaz Vs. Md. Iftikher reported in AIR 1932 PC 76 held that: "Adopting the principle of Mohammedan Law as stated by this Board in Imambandi Vs. Mutsuddi their Lordships have no doubt that the courts in India were right in holding that Faizunnessa had no authority to enter into the agreement of reference on behalf of the plaintiffs, who were minors at that time, so as to make the award binding on them as to their share in the immoveable property of their father." Earlier to the said decision Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the case of Mir Sarwajan Vs. Fakaruddin reported in 39 IA 1 observed that : They are, however, of opinion that it is not within the competence of the manager of a minor's estate or within the competence of a guardian of a minor to bind the minor or minor's estate by a contract for the purchase of immoveable property and they are further of opinion that as the minor in the present case was not bound by the contract, there was no mutuality and that the minor who has now reached his majority cannot obtain specific performance of the contract". Following the decisions in the case of Imambandi and Mir Sarwarjan a Division Bench of the Patna High Court in the case of Abdul Haq Vs. Md. Yahiya Khan reported in 78 IC 483 refused specific performance of contract for sale against minors and in that case Das J observed as follows: 

 "Defendant No. 2 as the de facto guardian of defendant Nos. 3 and 4 had no power to convey to the plaintiff the shares of the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 in the properties agreed to be sold. "It was further observed regarding Imambandi's case "It is quite true that was not a case of specific performance but the principle is equally applicable to a case where the de facto quardian has entered into a contract with a third party for the sale of minor's property The decision of the Judicial Committee in Mir Sarwarjan Vs. Fakhuddin Mahamud is, in my opinion, final and decisive". A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court in the case of Sreenath Vs. latindra Mohan reported in 30 CWN 263 refused to distinguish the decision in the case of Mir Sarwarjan with the following observations: "We cannot see, however, that there is any such distinction to be found from the perusal of the judgment to which I have referred to. The ruling, it seems to us, lays down the law in unequivocal terms and is binding on us. We think, therefore, having regard to this decision the first point must prevail and there could be no specific performance of a contract so far as defendant No. 6 (minor) is concerned." 

 Relying upon these facts the learned Advocate for the respondent strenuously argued that since the defendant No. 1 got herself appointed guardian and also obtained the permission in pursuance of agreement Ext. 1 the transaction in question by implication and conduct of the defendant No. 1 was ratified and as such the same is specifically enforceable. In support of his contention the learned Advocate relied on the decision of the Patna High Court in the case of Gobardhan Lal and others Vs. Sheo Narayan Sahu reported in 417 IC 161=AIR 1928 Patna 206. In that case a certificated guardian entered into a contract for sale of the minors property to the plaintiff of that suit and subsequently obtained permission of the court for effecting the said sale to the said plaintiff. In that case it was held as follows: 

 "It is obvious, therefore, that a sale by certificated guardian in contravention of sections 28 and 29 of the Guardians and Wards Act is voidable and not void." 

 In view of the provisions of the Guardians and Wards Act court granted specific performance of contract against the minors in that case. But facts of that case are distinguishable from the facts of the present case. In the present case Ext. 1 was executed by the defendant No. 1 before her appointment as guardian of the minors. We have already observed that she was nothing but a da facto guardian having no power to enter into contract for sale of the interest of the minor 'defendants at the time of execution of the agreement Ext. 1 and as such the same was void against the minors and no question of approval of the same arose. 

 13. The question of ratification of an alienation of an immoveable property belonging to a Mohammedan minor by the de facto guardian of the minor came up for consideration before a Full Bench of the Allahabad High Court in the case of Mt. Anto Vs. Mt. Reoti Kuar and others reported in AIR .1936 (Alillhabad) 337. In that case it was held that a transaction amounting to an alienation of an immoveable property belonging to a Mohammedan minor by the de facto guardian of the minor is void and as such there can be no question of ratification of the transaction by the minor upon his attaining majority. Similar question was raised in the case of Mohammad Ejaj Hossain Vs. Mohammad Iftikhar already referred to. In that case it was contended on behalf of the respondent that the mother of the minors who executed the agreement of reference for arbitration on behalf of her minor children was subsequently appointed guardian of the person and property of her minor children and as such it should be presumed that the said agreement of reference was approved by the court appointing her guardian. Such contention was negatived on the ground that the agreement of reference was not brought to the notice of the court appointing the guardian. We have already noticed in the present case that neither in the Act VIII case nor in the permission case the agreement Ext. 1 was brought to the notice of the court. We are, therefore, of the view that from the mere fact that the de facto guardian, defendant No.1 was subsequently appointed certificated guardian and granted permission to sell minors share of the suit property without mentioning the name of the buyer it cannot be said that the court approved the agreement Ext. 1 to sell minors share of the suit property to the plaintiff. 

 14. Our Appellate Division in the case of Archana Prasad Nandi Vs. Miss Chilia Randolph and others reported in 1982 BLD (AD) 90 considered the question of specific performance of a contract entered into by two major and one minor defendants represented by her mother who was not her guardian appointed by court. In that case both the courts below dismissed the plaintiff`s suit for specific performance of contract. On appeal a Single Judge of the High Court Division upheld that decisions of the courts below but directed return of the earnest money. On further appeal by the plaintiff Appellate Division decreed the suit in part against the major defendant Nos. 1 + 3 in respect of their 2/3 rd share on payment of the full purchase money and refused specific performance against the minor defendant No. 2 in respect of her 1/3 rd share on the view that the contract on behalf of the minor defendant No. 2 by her mother defendant No. 3 was void.
